Date: 2026-03-27

Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Martinez (CTO - Orion Newco), Priya Singh (ML Engineer), Liam O'Neill (Head of Platform)
summary: Intro discovery covering Redwood PLG quickstart, free credits, time-to-first-token expectations, and high-level guardrails for moving from hosted API to Dedicated/Private. Customer cares about latency, data residency, and SSO. Agreed next steps: share quickstart + pricing, run small benchmark, schedule technical deep dive.
topics: Intro and goals; current stack and pain points; PLG quickstart and free credits; hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs; security/compliance questions (SOC2/KMS/VPC); benchmarking and time-to-first-token; next steps & actions.
transcript:
00:00 Jamie Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jamie from Redwood, this is Ravi on the SE side. Uh, quick roll call?
00:08 Alex Martinez: Hey Alex here. Priya and Liam also with me.
00:12 Priya Singh: Hi all.
00:14 Ravi Patel: Great. So goal for today is to understand your use-case, answer questions about the quickstart, and how you might move from hosted to dedicated/private later.
00:25 Alex Martinez: Yeah, main thing for us is time-to-first-token, and cost. We're prototyping a semantic search + assistants feature, want to know how fast we can get something in prod.
00:36 Jamie Chen: Awesome. Priya, can you share your current infra briefly?
00:40 Priya Singh: Sure. We run a microservices stack on EKS, our embeddings pipeline is on a few g4-like nodes right now. We're using OpenAI in prod for prototypes but cost is creeping up. Latency is an issue for interactive flows, 300-400ms p50 is our goal.
00:57 Ravi Patel: Cool, that's helpful. With Redwood PLG quickstart we aim for time-to-first-token in the minutes — you can sign up self-serve, get free credits, and call the hosted API. The SDK has a sample that gets you up and running in like 10 minutes, realistically a dev can get tokens flowing in under an hour.
01:16 Liam O'Neill: When you say free credits, is that something for startups only or available to trial accounts? And how much are we talking?
01:24 Jamie Chen: Good q. We give free credits for quick evaluation — typically enough to run a few thousand tokens worth of calls. For enterprise pilots we often provide more targeted credits. I'll include the exact promo details in the follow-up.
01:36 Alex Martinez: Ok. Also curious about Dedicated — if we outgrow hosted, how hard is migration? We want predictable throughput and data isolation.
01:45 Ravi Patel: Migration is designed to be smooth. Same API surface. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and SLA-backed latency/throughput. For private/VPC we give a private control plane and can help with initial deploy. The main differences are networking and operational ownership.
01:59 Priya Singh: Any gotchas with KV cache or prefix caching? We saw docs mention KV cache but need clarity on how state is managed in multi-tenant hosted mode.
02:09 Ravi Patel: In hosted we have tenant-level KV caching and prefix cache, but to address isolation needs we can pin you to dedicated capacity or private. Sometimes the wording in the docs is fuzzy — sorry if it's unclear — we call it KV cache but often transcribed as KV cash in older notes.
02:23 Alex Martinez: ha — noted. Security wise we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration. Are these supported in hosted?
02:31 Jamie Chen: Hosted supports RBAC and audit logs for enterprise customers; SOC2 is in place for our platform. For KMS and customer-managed keys that's typically part of Dedicated or Private models but we do have integrations for hosted enterprise tiers. I'll attach the security pack PDF.
02:47 Liam O'Neill: Data residency? Our legal asks data not to leave EU. Does Redwood host regions in EU for hosted customers?
02:53 Ravi Patel: Yes, we have EU region endpoints. For strict residency the Private deployment inside your VPC or on-premises is the safest route.
03:03 Priya Singh: For our bench tests, we want to simulate our request distribution, including long context sequences ~2k tokens. How does Redwood handle long context with quantized models?
03:14 Ravi Patel: Our runtime supports quantization paths and kernel selection tuned for long sequences. You'll want to try a Dedicated profile for sustained low-latency long-context workloads. We'll provide model profiles and recommend quantization settings for your seq length.
03:29 Alex Martinez: Great. Can you run a quick walkthrough of the quickstart? Just the steps we care about: create account, get API key, run a sample request.
03:36 Jamie Chen: Yep. 1) Sign up at console.redwood.ai -> quickstart project. 2) Claim free credits. 3) Install SDK or curl example; sample code in the quickstart repo. 4) Hit /v1/generate with your API key and you'll stream tokens back. I'll paste the exact curl.
03:53 Speaker 1: (mumble) do you have a sample for streaming and function calling?
03:57 Ravi Patel: Yes — streaming and function/tool calling are supported. We'll share sample repo with both streaming and structured output examples.
04:06 Priya Singh: And what about rate limits for trial accounts? We get throttled a lot in some providers which hurts perf testing.
04:13 Jamie Chen: Trials have conservative rate limits but we're flexible for pilot customers; we can bump limits for your test window — request it in the follow-up and we'll provision.
04:24 Alex Martinez: For benchmarking, we'd like to compare hosted Redwood against our current OpenAI spend — can Redwood run a small A/B with same prompt set?
04:33 Ravi Patel: Yes, we can help with a benchmark runbook and scripts to replay your prompts. We'll also show cost per token and latency breakdowns in the Console.
04:44 Priya Singh: Any known issues with SDKs? We primarily use Python and node.
04:48 Jamie Chen: SDKs are first-class for Python, Node, Go; most customers use Python SDK for integration. There are community examples for Rails and others.
04:56 Liam O'Neill: Ok, what's the timeline if we wanted to run a pilot — say two-week pilot to validate perf and cost?
05:02 Jamie Chen: Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks. For hosted quickstart you can start immediately with free credits, then we recommend a 2-week benchmark with bumped rate limits. If you need Dedicated, provisioning can take a few weeks depending on capacity and contractual terms.
05:17 Alex Martinez: Pricing — what's the rough delta between hosted and Dedicated? Our controllers want numbers.
05:22 Jamie Chen: Hosted is pay-as-you-go (per-token + embeddings). Dedicated has a reserved capacity component (monthly commit) but lower unit costs at scale. I'll send a pricing sheet with examples that map to the throughput you described.
05:33 Priya Singh: Are there any legal contracts around data usage? We need to ensure no model training on our data.
05:38 Jamie Chen: We do not use customer data to continue training models by default. We'll include the data processing addendum in the security pack.
05:46 Speaker 2: (background) sorry — small interruption.
05:49 Ravi Patel: no worries. Back to bench: can you outline success criteria for the pilot?
05:56 Alex Martinez: Sure — 1) p50 latency <300ms for short prompts, 2) cost per query below our current baseline, 3) no PII leakage, and 4) integration work minimal (less than 2 dev-weeks).
06:12 Jamie Chen: That's helpful. We'll map those to the pilot plan.
06:16 Priya Singh: One more technical: for embeddings at scale do you recommend pre-computation + cache vs on-demand?
06:21 Ravi Patel: Pre-compute is usually cheaper; we also offer caching layers and embedding store integrations. For dynamic content, incremental updates with caching hits are recommended.
06:31 Alex Martinez: Great. Let's talk next steps.
06:34 Jamie Chen: We'll: 1) Send quickstart guide + exact free credits terms, 2) Share benchmark runbook and sample scripts, 3) Provision trial rate-limit bump for a 2-week window, 4) Schedule a technical deep dive week of Apr 5th — does that work?
06:50 Priya Singh: Apr 5th looks good for us.
06:53 Liam O'Neill: Works here.
06:55 Alex Martinez: Thanks everyone.
06:56 Jamie Chen: Thanks, talk soon.
